_meta.indication: Amyvid is indicated for PET imaging of the brain to estimate β-amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment being evaluated for Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and other causes of cognitive decline; a negative scan is inconsistent with a neuropathological diagnosis of AD at the time of image acquisition.
_meta.receipt_date: October 7, 2011 (resubmission / complete response to the March 17, 2011 action letter)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study A07, a Phase III study of the correlation between florbetapir F 18 PET imaging and amyloid pathology (autopsy cohort = Study One)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Single Phase 3 study imaging end-of-life patients, correlating premortem Amyvid PET amyloid burden (semi-quantitative visual rating, median of 3 readers) against the autopsy histopathology (quantitative IHC) truth standard.
pivotal_trials.population: Autopsy cohort: adults with a projected life expectancy of ≤ 6 months (152 imaged, 29 included in the primary efficacy analysis).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Correlation between patient-level amyloid burden on Amyvid PET (semi-quantitative visual rating 0-4, median of 3 readers) and cortical amyloid burden by quantitative IHC histopathology.
pivotal_trials.n: 29 autopsy-cohort subjects in the primary efficacy analysis (152 imaged)
pivotal_trials.result: Autopsy cohort primary endpoint met: statistically significant correlation with Spearman's ρ=0.78, p<0.0001 in the 29 subjects.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study PT01 (Study Three) — reader-training validation / image re-read study with web-based training
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Image re-read / reader-training validation study (submitted in the resubmission cycle)
pivotal_trials.design: 5 nuclear-medicine readers, trained with the proposed web-based program and reading in their own facilities, interpreted a pooled set of 151 scans (59 autopsy, 20 normal control, 52 MCI, 20 AD) as positive/negative versus the autopsy CERAD truth standard.
pivotal_trials.population: Pooled images of 151 subjects: 59 autopsy (truth standard), 20 normal controls, 52 MCI, and 20 AD.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: inter-reader/intra-reader agreement (Fleiss' kappa) using web-based reader training; secondary: sensitivity and specificity versus autopsy histopathology truth standard.
pivotal_trials.n: 151 scans read by 5 readers (59 autopsy subjects provided the truth standard)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary and secondary objectives met: inter-reader Fleiss' kappa 0.83 (95% CI 0.78 to 0.88) for all 151 scans; median sensitivity 82% and median specificity 95% versus the histopathology truth standard.

key_safety: No serious adverse reactions; most commonly reported adverse reactions (N=496) were headache 9 (1.8%), musculoskeletal pain 4 (0.8%), fatigue 3 (0.6%), and nausea 3 (0.6%).
target_moa: Florbetapir F 18 is a molecular imaging agent that binds to β-amyloid aggregates/plaques; the F 18 isotope produces a positron signal detected by a PET scanner, with differential retention in brain areas containing β-amyloid (in vitro Kd = 3.7 ± 0.3 nM).
modality: Radiopharmaceutical (F-18 PET radioactive diagnostic imaging agent)

advisory_committee.vote: At the January 20, 2011 Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee (original cycle), the committee voted 13 to 3 to recommend against approval due to deficiencies in image-interpretation (reader training) methods, but voted 16 to 0 that, with an adequate training program, the data would support approval.

description.text: Removed limitations of use and added indication for selection of patients indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy; added quantitative image analysis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section of the prescribing information by removing the limitations of use and adding a new indication, specifically, use for selection of patients who are indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy as described in the prescribing information of the therapeutic products. In addition, the use of quantitative image analysis is added to the Image Display and Interpretation subsection of the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION section.

summary.text: Amyvid (florbetapir F 18) was submitted as a 505(b) NDA and reviewed under priority review in its original cycle; FDA issued a Complete Response letter on March 17, 2011 citing clinical (reader-training), manufacturing, and facility deficiencies. Following an October 7, 2011 complete-response resubmission adding the PT01 reader-training validation study, it was approved on April 6, 2012 as a standard (class 2) resubmission with two postmarketing commitments.

The sponsor submitted a response to the CR letter of March, 2011. The main feature within the response was the submission of Study PT01 results that verified Amyvid scans can be accurately and reproducibly interpreted by conventional imaging professionals.

requirement.text: PMC 1887-1: Conduct a clinical study comparing Amyvid scan interpretations at local clinical sites to interpretations by expert(s) at a central reading facility, to assess the impact of reader training methods on reliability in clinical practice.

citations.quote: **1887-1:** To conduct a clinical study that will compare the results of Amyvid scan interpretations at local clinical sites to interpretations performed by an expert(s) at a central reading facility. The main objectives of this study are to assess the impact of different reader training methods on the reliability of Amyvid scan interpretations as they are performed in clinical practice and to help determine the performance of the reader training processes as compared to the experts at the central reading facility.

requirement.text: PMC 1887-2: Conduct a clinical study exploring the use of standard uptake value ratio (SUVR) and/or other quantitative outcomes as an alternative or adjunct to qualitative Amyvid scan interpretations.

citations.quote: **1887-2:** To conduct a clinical study that will explore the use of standard uptake value ratio (SUVR) and/or other quantitative outcomes as an alternative or an adjunct to qualitative Amyvid scan interpretations. The main objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of implementing a quantitative process for Amyvid scan interpretation by clinical sites, and to measure the resulting reliability of scan interpretations.
